source_review.notes: Reviewed eight sources covering parallel data partitioning, consistent hashing, Dynamo, Spanner, workload-driven partitioning, application auto-sharding, geo-distributed shard management, and durable distributed-data design. ACM DOI metadata confirmed four paper identities and dates; USENIX and PVLDB primary publication pages were retrieved for three papers. No current vendor behavior or mutable product limit is asserted.

evidence: Reviewed key-space, logical-partition, epoch-versioned placement, resource-weight, load, capacity, utilization, fault-set, movement, and heavy-hitter notation.
Confirmed load and capacity use the same resource dimension before division and that coefficient of variation is used only for positive mean load.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The chapter explicitly rejects collapsing multidimensional feasibility into one scalar score.

evidence: Recomputed loads [40,20,20,20]: mean 25, population variance 75, standard deviation 8.660254, and CV 0.346410.
Recomputed 1,200,000 MB divided by 40 MB/s as 30,000 seconds, or 8.333 hours under the stated decimal simplification.
Recomputed exercise loads [60,30,20,10]: mean 30, population variance 350, standard deviation 18.708287, CV 0.623610, and maximum-to-mean ratio 2.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Movement duration is explicitly an optimistic lower bound excluding concurrent writes, validation, retries, and throttling.

evidence: Verified partition load as the sum of weights mapped to each partition and normalized utilization as load divided by safe capacity.
Verified the population coefficient-of-variation expression and its application to the two worked distributions.
Verified T greater than or equal to B/b as a transfer lower bound when B and b use compatible units.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: No balance statistic is presented as a capacity, tail-latency, placement-independence, or safety proof.

evidence: Reviewed monotonic range hotspot, read-heavy celebrity key, whale tenant, global scatter-gather, cross-shard money transfer, and oversized movement unit.
Reviewed target crash, stale routing cache, dual owner, delayed tombstone, policy change during move, correlated zone label, saturated repair, and rollback.
Reviewed residency across primary, backup, log, cache, transit, repair, support, and restored-snapshot paths.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Cases span workload, correctness, capacity, failure-domain, governance, security, recovery, and physical-world boundaries.

evidence: Traced unique partition authority, routing/storage epoch agreement, stale-writer rejection, rights conservation, replica anti-affinity, residency, and deletion preservation through exposition and examples.
Confirmed rebalancing and repair preserve foreground reserve and do not establish completion until indexes, streams, tombstones, external effects, and business outcomes reconcile.
invariant_checking.notes: Logical identity remains separate from physical placement throughout migration and recovery.

evidence: Reviewed the balance derivation and confirmed squared deviations and population divisor match the declared formula.
Reviewed the movement lower bound and confirmed it is conditioned on safe residual rate rather than nominal link capacity.
Reviewed the hot-key counterexample and confirmed adding placements cannot divide one unchanged serial ownership key.
proof_review.notes: Probabilistic hash balance, migration safety, and failure independence are never claimed from arithmetic alone.

evidence: Audited uses of authoritative, stable, balanced, safe, independent, local, current, copied, complete, resilient, and residency-compliant.
Verified models, lower bounds, mechanisms, policies, observations, business invariants, and empirical tests retain explicit scopes.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Host labels, replica counts, row counts, and matching bytes are not treated as conclusive evidence.

empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The chapter prescribes workload traces, heavy-hitter measurements, history tests, and migration experiments but reports no executed distributed deployment or benchmark.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed logical and physical mappings, access and invariant boundaries, range/hash/directory/composite keys, multidimensional skew, hot keys, fan-out, granularity, replica placement, residency, colocation, epoch authority, online movement, headroom, metadata failure, tenant isolation, observability, and adversarial evolution for coherence.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed order-ingest hotspot, weighted imbalance, celebrity reads, account transfer, 1.2-TB move, correlated replicas, health-data residency, dual ownership, 2,000-way fan-out, and production-impacting rebalance. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified graduate-depth models and operational protocols, sixteen misconceptions, ten distinct worked examples, and five progressive exercises with complete answers ending in an unfamiliar international emergency-supply placement problem.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed. Source checks and calculations do not constitute a live sharding, migration, correlated-failure, jurisdiction, disaster, or emergency-supply experiment.
